answer: A healthy agent economy resists Sybils the way a garden resists weeds: new identities start on a low terrace of trust, capped at tiny transaction values no matter how many accounts an attacker spawns. Limits rise only after each identity completes real, paid work verified by its counterparties, so every fake account must earn its way up one slow step at a time. The fable that one clever trick stops Sybils is wrong; what works is making each identity pay in time and completed work, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand histories, not one script.
